title: Boss: login with OpenID Connect
summary: Write both sides of an OIDC login: a client that starts and finishes the flow safely, and an identity provider with discovery, PKCE and id_tokens.

steps.title: Both sides of the redirect
body: You will build the two halves of an OpenID Connect login:
1. **The client**: start a login with fresh `state`, `nonce` and PKCE verifier; handle the callback by checking `state` and preparing the token request.
2. **The identity provider**: discovery document, `/authorize` with PKCE and `openid` required, and `/token` returning an access token for the API and an id_token for the client.
3. **Back at the client**: verify the id_token that came back.

steps.title: The client side
prompt: - `AuthClient(string authority, string clientId, string redirectUri)`. A trailing `/` on `authority` must not produce `//authorize`.
- `string StartLogin(string[] scopes)`: creates a random `state` (16 bytes), `nonce` (16 bytes) and PKCE verifier (32 bytes), all base64url, remembers them, and returns

`{authority}/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=..&redirect_uri=..&scope=..&state=..&nonce=..&code_challenge=..&code_challenge_method=S256` (escape client id, redirect URI and scope with `Uri.EscapeDataString`).

- `Dictionary<string, string>? HandleCallback(string callbackUrl)`: parse the query of `https://app/callback?code=..&state=..`. Return `null` if there's an `error` parameter, no `code`, or the `state` is unknown. Check for `error` first: an error callback leaves its state pending. Each state works **once** for a real callback. Otherwise return the form for `/token`: `grant_type`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `code_verifier`.
- `string? NonceFor(string state)`: the nonce remembered for a state still pending (so the id_token can be checked), else `null`.
starter: public AuthClient(string authority, string clientId, string redirectUri) { }
public Dictionary<string, string>? HandleCallback(string callbackUrl) => null;
solution: private readonly Dictionary<string, (string Verifier, string Nonce)> _pending = new();
public AuthClient(string authority, string clientId, string redirectUri)
if (!query.TryGetValue("state", out var state) || !_pending.Remove(state, out var pending)) return null;
if (!query.TryGetValue("code", out var code)) return null;
public string? NonceFor(string state) => _pending.TryGetValue(state, out var p) ? p.Nonce : null;
hints: Keep a `Dictionary<string, (string Verifier, string Nonce)>` keyed by state.
`new Uri(callbackUrl).Query` gives `?code=..&state=..`; split on `&` and `=` and unescape the values.
`_pending.Remove(state, out var pending)` makes each state single-use.
template: string Q(string url, string name) => new Uri(url).Query.TrimStart('?').Split('&').Select(p => p.Split('=', 2)).Where(p => p[0] == name).Select(p => Uri.UnescapeDataString(p[1])).FirstOrDefault() ?? "";
Dojo.Check("the URL starts with the authorize endpoint", dojoUrl.StartsWith("https://id.dojo/authorize?response_type=code&"), dojoUrl);
Dojo.Check("state is random and long enough", dojoState.Length >= 22, dojoState);
Dojo.Eq("NonceFor(state) matches the URL", Q(dojoUrl, "nonce"), dojoC.NonceFor(dojoState));
Dojo.Check("a second login gets a different state", Q(dojoC.StartLogin(["openid"]), "state") != dojoState, "same state");
Dojo.Eq("a callback with an unknown state -> null", null, dojoC.HandleCallback("https://notes.example/callback?code=abc&state=forged"));
Dojo.Eq("a callback with an error -> null", null, dojoC.HandleCallback("https://notes.example/callback?error=access_denied&state=" + dojoState));
Dojo.Check("a good callback returns the token form", dojoForm is not null, "got null");
Dojo.Eq("the verifier hashes to the challenge that was sent", Q(dojoUrl, "code_challenge"), B64(SHA256.HashData(System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(dojoVer))));
Dojo.Eq("the same state can't be used twice", null, dojoC.HandleCallback("https://notes.example/callback?code=SplxlOBeZQ&state=" + dojoState));

steps.title: The identity provider
prompt: The starter has a registered client `notes-spa` (redirect `https://notes.example/callback`), a code store, and `MakeJwt(object)` for HS256 tokens. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.

| `POST /authorize` (JSON `AuthorizeRequest`) | registered client and exact redirect, `S256` -> else `400 invalid_request`; `scope` must include `openid` -> else `400 invalid_scope`; store a `Grant`; `200 {code, state}` |

| `POST /token` (form) | as in the PKCE lesson (`unsupported_grant_type`, single-use code, matching `client_id` and `redirect_uri`, S256 check of `code_verifier` -> else `400 invalid_grant`). On success, with `sub` = the `User` who consented: `access_token` = JWT `{iss, sub, aud: "notes-api", scope, iat, exp}`, `id_token` = JWT `{iss, sub, aud: <client id>, iat, exp, nonce}` (nonce only if one was sent), `token_type`, `expires_in: 600`, `scope` |
starter: IResult OAuthError(string error, int status = 400) => Results.Json(new { error }, statusCode: status);
record AuthorizeRequest(string? ClientId, string? RedirectUri, string? Scope, string? State, string? Nonce,
string? CodeChallenge, string? CodeChallengeMethod, string? User);
record Grant(string ClientId, string RedirectUri, string Challenge, string User, string? Nonce, string Scope);
solution: IResult OAuthError(string error, int status = 400) => Results.Json(new { error }, statusCode: status);
if (req.ClientId is null || !clients.TryGetValue(req.ClientId, out var uri) || uri != req.RedirectUri) return OAuthError("invalid_request");
codes[code] = new Grant(req.ClientId, req.RedirectUri!, req.CodeChallenge, req.User ?? "", req.Nonce, string.Join(' ', scopes));
if (!codes.TryRemove(form["code"].ToString(), out var g)) return OAuthError("invalid_grant");
if (form["client_id"] != g.ClientId || form["redirect_uri"] != g.RedirectUri) return OAuthError("invalid_grant");
var access = MakeJwt(new { iss = Issuer, sub = g.User, aud = "notes-api", scope = g.Scope, iat = now, exp = now + 600 });
var idClaims = new Dictionary<string, object> { ["iss"] = Issuer, ["sub"] = g.User, ["aud"] = g.ClientId, ["iat"] = now, ["exp"] = now + 600 };
if (g.Nonce is not null) idClaims["nonce"] = g.Nonce;
return Results.Ok(new { access_token = access, id_token = MakeJwt(idClaims), token_type = "Bearer", expires_in = 600, scope = g.Scope });
record AuthorizeRequest(string? ClientId, string? RedirectUri, string? Scope, string? State, string? Nonce,
string? CodeChallenge, string? CodeChallengeMethod, string? User);
record Grant(string ClientId, string RedirectUri, string Challenge, string User, string? Nonce, string Scope);
hints: Return a `Dictionary<string, object>` from the discovery endpoint so the snake_case names come out exactly.
Reuse your PKCE token endpoint; build the id_token claims in a `Dictionary<string, object>` so `nonce` can be added only when present.

Dojo.Eq("id_token aud is the client", "notes-spa", DojoWeb.Prop(id, "aud"));
Dojo.Eq("access_token aud is the API", "notes-api", DojoWeb.Prop(at, "aud"));

steps.title: Finish the login
prompt: The client got a token response back. Write `string? CompleteLogin(string tokenResponseJson, byte[] key, string issuer, string clientId, string expectedNonce, long now)` that returns the user's `sub`, or `null` if anything is wrong:
- the response has an `id_token` that is an HS256 JWT (header `alg` = `HS256`) signed with `key` (constant-time compare),
- its `iss` equals `issuer`, its `aud` equals `clientId` (a string here), `now < exp`, and `nonce` equals `expectedNonce`.
Never throw. The tests import `System.Security.Cryptography` and `System.Text.Json`.
starter: string? CompleteLogin(string tokenResponseJson, byte[] key, string issuer, string clientId, string expectedNonce, long now)
solution: case 1: throw new FormatException("Not valid base64url.");
string? CompleteLogin(string tokenResponseJson, byte[] key, string issuer, string clientId, string expectedNonce, long now)
if (!response.RootElement.TryGetProperty("id_token", out var idEl) || idEl.GetString() is not string idToken) return null;
if (!header.RootElement.TryGetProperty("alg", out var alg) || alg.GetString() != "HS256") return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("iss", out var iss) || iss.GetString() != issuer) return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("aud", out var aud) || aud.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || aud.GetString() != clientId) return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("exp", out var exp) || now >= exp.GetInt64()) return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("nonce", out var nonce) || nonce.GetString() != expectedNonce) return null;
return p.TryGetProperty("sub", out var sub) ? sub.GetString() : null;
catch (Exception e) when (e is FormatException or JsonException or InvalidOperationException)
hints: Parse the response, then reuse your HS256 verification from the JWT module.
Check the four claims with early `return null`s.
template: Dojo.Eq("a good response -> ada", "ada", CompleteLogin(Resp(Id(Good)), K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("no id_token -> null", null, CompleteLogin("{\"access_token\":\"x\"}", K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("signed with another key -> null", null, CompleteLogin(Resp(DojoJwt.Hs(Good, new byte[32])), K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("alg none -> null", null, CompleteLogin(Resp(DojoJwt.B64("{\"alg\":\"none\"}") + "." + DojoJwt.B64(Good) + "."), K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("wrong issuer -> null", null, CompleteLogin(Resp(Id(Good)), K, "https://other.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("an id_token for another client -> null", null, CompleteLogin(Resp(Id(Good)), K, "https://id.dojo", "other-spa", "n-1", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("nonce from another login -> null", null, CompleteLogin(Resp(Id(Good)), K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-2", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("not JSON -> null", null, CompleteLogin("oops", K, "https://id.dojo", "notes-spa", "n-1", 1000));
